name: Evolution — Living Population
description: Fig 11b — evolution by natural selection as a genuine place-graph rewrite you can play forward. A `population` (tree[node]) of identically-schema'd `cell` nodes — each carrying a heritable scalar `trait` and a derived `division_rate` — evolves under an `environment` whose `selection_optimum` slowly DRIFTS over time (a moving target). Each generation the optimum shifts, each cell's division rate is re-scored by how close its trait sits to the current optimum (a Gaussian fitness kernel), and cells undergo BINARY FISSION: a dividing cell is REPLACED by two daughters, each inheriting its trait ± Gaussian mutation (so the founder does not persist once it has divided). The population grows to carrying capacity; beyond it, the least-fit cells (furthest from the optimum) die. Over many generations the whole trait cloud tracks the drifting optimum — selection + mutation + division, the minimal Darwinian loop. Running it adds/removes place-graph nodes and shifts the optimum leaf each tick — steppable topology for the loom run/animate feature.

drift.description: Shift of the environment's selection optimum per generation (the moving target).

sel_strength.description: Selection sharpness — the Gaussian fitness width (fitness = e^{-s·Δ²}).

mut_sigma.description: Standard deviation of the heritable mutation step passed to each daughter.

div_rate.description: Per-generation division probability for a perfectly-fit cell.
